en: Taal Volcano's main crater contains Vulcan Point, an island inside a lake inside a volcano.
Mount Pinatubo's 1991 eruption was the second-largest volcanic eruption on Earth during the twentieth century.
Lake Mainit in Mindanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, reaching a maximum depth of 223 meters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical cone-shaped hills that turn brown during the dry season.
Although the Philippines has 7,641 islands, only about 2,000 of them are actually inhabited by people.
The province of Davao Oriental is the easternmost point in the Philippines, closest to the Pacific Ocean.
The Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones annually because it sits in the Pacific Typhoon Belt.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines and is home to the critically endangered Philippine eagle.
The Tamaraw, a small dwarf buffalo, is an endangered animal found exclusively in the wild on Mindoro island.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site located in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest known mineral deposits, including vast reserves of gold, copper, and nickel.
